title: Predictive credit pools for tenant-level fairness and graceful degradation
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: Dedicated fleets see bursty tenant traffic that either starves other tenants during bursts or causes the fleet to over-provision. Current admission shapers are static or reactive and do not leverage short-term demand forecasts, causing unnecessary shedding or long queues.

Goal: Build a predictive credit-pool admission controller that: (1) allocates per-tenant credit budgets based on short-term demand forecasts and long-term SLA commitments, (2) exposes soft burst windows that allow temporary exceedance without violating fleet-wide throughput guarantees, and (3) integrates with autoscaler signals and model-variant fallbacks to perform graceful degradation rather than hard drops. This should improve fairness, reduce tail latency for SLO-bound tenants, and reduce unnecessary autoscaler churn.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant credit pools allocate credits such that 95% of tenant bursts up to configured burst_window are served without shedding when fleet headroom exists
When fleet headroom is low, controller performs prioritized degradation: first route to cached/quantized variants, then soft-throttle, then shed; documented fallback order configurable per-tenant
End-to-end tests show P95 latency for SLO tenants stays within 1.2x baseline under a 3x burst from top 10% tenants
Fairness metric (Jain's index computed across tenant throughput over 5m windows) improves by >10% vs baseline controller in simulated mixed workload
Controller exposes observability signals (credit balance, forecasted demand, borrow events, degradation triggers) to Console and an SLO/alert rule is added
Design doc + RFC reviewed and approved by serving runtime and autoscaling owners; implementation PR merged and feature flagged
design_decisions: Use an EWMA-based short-term demand forecast (alpha configured per-tenant) rather than full ML model to keep controller simple and deterministic
Implement a tri-tier credit composition: baseline SLA credits (hard-guarantee), burst escrow (soft, borrowable when headroom exists), and headroom reserve (fleet-level safety buffer)
Credit replenishment cadence = 1s buckets to align with our admission path and reduce jitter; credits are fractional (float) to support sub-token granular allocation
Borrowing rules: tenants may borrow from fleet escrow up to per-tenant cap; borrowing increments a debt metric that must be repaid within repayment_window or be subject to priority penalties

Graceful degradation order: 1) route to model variant with lower compute (quantized/ distilled), 2) serve from KV cache/prefix cache when applicable, 3) apply soft-rate limit (queuing with deadline-aware dequeue), 4) final shed with informative rejection payload
Autoscaler interplay: controller emits predictive tail signals to autoscaler; autoscaler may provision transient capacity if predicted sustained demand > threshold for configurable horizon
progress_updates: 2025-11-05: Spike completed — validated EWMA forecast is sufficient for 1-5 minute horizon using representative tenant traces (spike test harness: /infra/bench/spike-harness). Results: 85% of bursts predicted within 20% error in 60s horizon

2025-11-12: Prototype credit pool implemented in admission-proxy branch 'predictive-credit-pools'. Local integration tests passed for single-fleet scenarios. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4127
2025-11-18: Design review with runtime and autoscaler teams. Feedback: add explicit repayment window and telemetry for borrow events. Action: updated RFC to include debt amortization schedule.

2025-11-24: Added graceful-degradation hooks to routing layer; can now route to quantized variants with per-tenant policy. E2E smoke tests show latencies fall back smoothly; PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/1023

2025-11-30: Canary rollout in dedicated-staging for 2 fleets; observed reduced hard-sheds but slight increase in instance churn due to autoscaler reacting to borrow-induced predictions. Meeting scheduled to tune autoscaler horizon and thresholds.
2025-12-02: Added Console charts for 'credit_balance' and 'borrow_events' and an alert when fleet-reserve < 10%. Observability PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/876
links: Incident postmortem reference for prior unfair shedding: https://docs.redwood.ai/incidents/2025-04-08-unplanned-shed-analysis
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Autoscaler may interpret borrow forecasts as sustained demand and over-provision. Mitigation: add amortization window and require multiple consecutive horizon breaches before scale-up trigger
Risk: Per-tenant debt could accumulate and allow noisy tenants to starve others. Mitigation: enforce hard debt caps and priority penalties; surface debt in Console for billing/ops
Risk: Increased controller complexity could add latency to admission path. Mitigation: keep critical path in optimized C++/Rust path and run forecast/credit accounting in fast, lock-free structures
next_steps: Tune EWMA alpha and burst_window per fleet based on canary telemetry
Introduce configurable repayments and per-tenant caps in UI and API
Iterate autoscaler integration to reduce unnecessary churn (require 2-min sustained prediction before scale-up)
Run 48h mixed-tenant soak tests and collect fairness, latency, and churn metrics
Prepare rollout plan and runbook for on-call when enabling feature in production fleets
